resources.title: Your Money, Your Goals: A Financial Empowerment Toolkit
resources.length: 241 pages (2020 edition), plus individual tools and handouts
resources.summary: A practical toolkit of worksheets and handouts on goal-setting, budgeting, emergency savings, debt, credit reports and choosing financial products. Built for people who help others with money questions, but most tools work just as well for individuals or adult-education classes.

resources.title: Youth Financial Education Classroom Activities
resources.length: 135 activities, each designed for a single class period
resources.summary: A searchable bank of short classroom activities, filterable by grade, duration and topic. Each comes with a teacher guide and student worksheets, so it can slot into a maths, English or social studies class as well as a personal finance course.

resources.title: Money Smart for Young Adults
resources.length: 12 modules, each with instructor guide, participant guide and slides
resources.licence: US federal government work; the FDIC describes Money Smart materials as non-copyrighted and free
resources.summary: A complete instructor-led course covering banking, saving, credit, borrowing, paying for college and protecting your identity. Ready to teach: every module includes the instructor script, the student guide and presentation slides.

resources.title: Money Smart (full programme for all ages)
resources.length: Several separate curricula plus 14 interactive games
resources.language: English (some materials also in Spanish and other languages)
resources.licence: US federal government work; the FDIC describes Money Smart materials as non-copyrighted and free
resources.summary: The hub for the FDIC's whole Money Smart family: curricula for young children through older adults, the 'How Money Smart Are You?' games, and a guide to running reality fairs where students make simulated life budget decisions.

resources.title: Saving and Investing for Students
resources.publisher: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) — Investor.gov
resources.summary: A plain-language introduction to making a financial plan, budgeting, saving and the basics of investing, including how to check out an investment so you don't fall for fraud or costly mistakes.

resources.title: Making Personal Finance Decisions
resources.licence: Free to use; published by the Federal Reserve System (not a federal-agency public-domain work — link only)
resources.summary: A high school curriculum that teaches personal finance through economic reasoning, using games and decision-making models — for example a 'wealth game' and an inventory game on net worth and cash flow.

resources.title: It's Your Paycheck
resources.licence: Free to use; published by the Federal Reserve System (link only)
resources.summary: Nine lessons on earning and keeping money: gross vs. net pay, reading W-2 and W-4 forms, credit rights and responsibilities, and the real cost of payday loans and rent-to-own deals.

resources.title: Next Gen Personal Finance (NGPF) curriculum
resources.length: Full semester course, middle school course, plus hundreds of standalone activities and case studies
resources.licence: Free to use; a free verified teacher account is needed for answer keys and assessments (link only)
resources.summary: One of the most widely used free personal finance curricula in US schools, run by a non-profit. Covers budgeting, banking, credit, paying for college, investing, taxes and behavioural economics, with ready-made lessons, projects and games.

resources.title: Khan Academy Financial Literacy course
resources.publisher: Khan Academy (non-profit), developed with funding from Capital One
resources.length: Self-paced course with 16 units, videos, articles and exercises
resources.summary: A free, self-paced course covering budgeting and saving, consumer credit, investing, taxes, insurance, and scams and fraud, with a teacher resources unit. Designed around the US financial system.

resources.title: Personal Finance (updated edition)
resources.publisher: LibreTexts — Coastline College (Guy Buker, Jerrie Muir and Erin Thomas), building on the original by Rachel S. Siegel and Carol Yacht
resources.summary: A modernised version of a long-established open personal finance textbook, updated for gig work, digital banking, student loan policy and doing your own financial research. Good as a free core text for an introductory college course.

resources.title: Personal Finance – Your Money, Your Life
resources.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (the book's own licence footer; link only — a different page on the same site describes it as CC BY 4.0, but the footer governs)
resources.summary: A recent (2025) open textbook focused on practical financial literacy, with real-world examples, case studies and exercises.

resources.title: Principles of Finance
resources.publisher: OpenStax (Rice University) — Julie Dahlquist and Rainford Knight, senior contributing authors
resources.length: Full textbook, 20 chapters, with Excel data exercises
resources.summary: A peer-reviewed introductory finance textbook — time value of money, financial statements, bonds and stocks. More business than personal finance, but useful for university students who want the theory behind everyday money decisions.

resources.title: Managing my money
resources.length: 24 hours of study over an 8-week course
resources.licence: CC BY-NC-SA (The Open University's standard OpenLearn licence; third-party materials within the course are excluded)
resources.summary: An eight-week introductory course on managing money day to day: compiling and using a budget, understanding debt and investment products, mortgage financing for home ownership, pension planning options, and insurance. Uses UK data and examples throughout its text, video and interactive content.

resources.title: You and your money
resources.licence: CC BY-NC-SA (The Open University's standard OpenLearn licence; third-party materials within the course are excluded)
resources.summary: An introductory course on household debt: how the financial services industry is structured, what financial liberalisation means, the basics of debt and interest calculations, different types of unsecured lending, and how to apply financial planning when deciding whether to borrow.

resources.title: Your Money, Your Goals Toolkit
resources.length: 43 tools and handouts across 10 topic categories
resources.summary: A set of 43 free tools and handouts across ten categories for facilitating money conversations: aligning spending with goals, reviewing credit reports, planning debt repayment, tracking income and bills, building savings, improving credit scores, choosing financial products, and avoiding fraud.

resources.title: Your Money, Your Goals: Booklets
resources.summary: Four downloadable booklets, each addressing one financial situation: falling behind on bills, managing existing debt, building credit after a setback, and working toward a savings goal. Each booklet covers tracking spending, prioritising action, and practical next steps for that situation.

resources.title: Adult Financial Education Tools & Resources
resources.type: Resource collection (handouts, worksheets, webinars, guides, booklets)
resources.length: 150+ resources across 13 topic areas and 6 audience categories; handouts typically 1-2 pages, booklets up to 20+ pages
resources.summary: A library of over 150 free handouts, worksheets, webinars, guides and sample letters organised by topic and audience, covering auto loans, credit, mortgages, debt, fraud, student loans and everyday money management for consumers, older adults, servicemembers and financial educators.

resources.title: Money Smart for Adults
resources.length: 14 modules, approximately 32 hours total (1 hour 25 minutes to 3 hours 50 minutes per module)
resources.language: English, Spanish, Chinese, Korean, Vietnamese, Braille and large print
resources.summary: A 14-module instructor-led curriculum covering money values, banking basics, budgeting, credit management, homebuying and disaster financial recovery, with scripted instructor guides, participant handouts, slides and trainer videos, available in English, Spanish, Chinese, Korean, Vietnamese, Braille and large print.

resources.title: Money Smart for Young People
resources.length: 6-22 lessons per grade band (PreK-2: 6; grades 3-5: 8; grades 6-8: 12; grades 9-12: 22)
resources.summary: A free K-12 financial literacy curriculum split by grade band: 6 lessons for PreK-2, 8 for grades 3-5, 12 for grades 6-8, and 22 for grades 9-12, moving from counting coins and needs versus wants to mortgages, retirement and entrepreneurship, in English and Spanish.

resources.title: Money Smart for Older Adults
resources.publisher: Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) and Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB)
resources.summary: A ten-module curriculum developed jointly by the FDIC and CFPB to help older adults and their caregivers prevent fraud, scams and financial exploitation, covering investment fraud, identity theft, charity and computer scams, and planning for financial emergencies. Free, in English and Spanish.

resources.title: Money Manual, Student Money Manual and teacher packs
resources.licence: Not stated (page footer carries a standard © 2026 The Money Charity copyright notice)
resources.summary: Three free downloadable guides from a UK financial education charity: a general Money Manual on managing everyday finances, a Student Money Manual on student finance and money at university, and interactive teacher resource packs for delivering financial education in schools.

resources.title: Financial Basics Workshop
resources.type: Workshop (downloadable materials and e-learning video series)
level: Young adults in post-secondary institutions, workplaces or community organisations
resources.length: Not stated (6 topic areas; separate self-paced e-learning video series)
resources.summary: A Canadian government workshop for young adults in post-secondary institutions, workplaces or community organisations, with downloadable presenter manuals, participant handbooks and slides covering budgeting, saving, credit, investing, fraud prevention and financial planning, plus a self-paced e-learning video series.

resources.title: Money Matters: Financial Literacy Workbooks
resources.licence: Not stated (page footer carries a standard © ABC Life Literacy Canada 2026 copyright notice)
resources.summary: A free introductory financial literacy program for adult learners, delivered through workbooks full of activities that organisations can adapt to a group's needs. Workshops can be run by an organisation's own staff or with support from volunteer tutors, in English or French.

resources.title: MoneySmart Publications & Resources
resources.publisher: Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) — Moneysmart
resources.length: Not stated (categorised list of downloadable factsheets; no total count given)
resources.language: English, plus separate resources translated into 10 languages
resources.summary: A hub of free downloadable factsheets on banking, budgeting, insurance, loans, debt, investing, super and complaints, plus a separate set of resources translated into 10 languages explaining core money concepts for newly arrived migrants to Australia.

resources.title: MoneySmart Lesson Plans
resources.publisher: Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) — Moneysmart
resources.summary: Ten free lesson plans from Lower Primary to Senior Secondary, created with ACARA and aligned to the Australian Curriculum version 9.0, on topics such as understanding coins, budgeting for a party, advertising, compound interest, spotting scams and investing basics.

resources.title: Tax, Super + You: Resource Library
resources.type: Resource library (activities, case studies, calculators, videos, worksheets)
resources.licence: Not stated (page footer carries a standard © Commonwealth of Australia notice)
resources.summary: An Australian Taxation Office library of 1,361 teaching resources — activities, case studies, calculators, videos and worksheets — for year 7 through senior secondary students, covering tax and superannuation within subjects including civics, work studies, history and mathematics.

resources.title: Education resources (Money Anthology)
resources.type: Teaching resources (lesson plans, interactive tools, videos, podcast)
resources.length: Not stated (approximately a dozen resource collections)
resources.licence: Not stated (page footer carries a standard ©2026 Bank of England notice)
resources.summary: Free teaching and homeschooling resources from the Bank of England explaining how the economy works and what the Bank does, including lesson plans and schemes of work for ages 5 to 16+, interactive calculators and converters, a video series and a podcast.

resources.title: Money and Me and Lessons from the Financial Crisis
resources.length: 'Money and Me': 12 lessons; 'Lessons from the Financial Crisis': 6 lessons; EconoME: 4 lessons; plus videos, games and worksheets
resources.licence: Not stated (page footer carries a standard ©2026 Bank of England notice)
resources.summary: A home learning hub including a 12-lesson 'Money and Me' scheme, a six-lesson scheme on the financial crisis, and the four-lesson EconoME programme, for ages 5 to 19, plus activity sheets, interactive games, videos and calculators from the Bank of England.

resources.title: Your Money Matters: financial education textbook
resources.length: Not stated (includes interactive activities and questions; 4 UK regional editions)
resources.language: English (versions for England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales)
resources.summary: A free, curriculum-mapped financial education textbook for UK secondary schools, in versions for England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales, with interactive activities and questions on savings and interest, budgeting, borrowing and debt, student finance, pensions, investing, and fraud and identity theft.

resources.title: Resource Hub (LifeSavers, Milo's Money and more)
resources.summary: A free resource hub from a UK charity offering school resources for financial decision-making lessons, family resources for home money conversations, and community resources, including the LifeSavers primary school savings programme, for teachers, parents and community organisations.

resources.title: HoweyTrade Investment Program Classroom Activity
resources.publisher: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) — Investor.gov
resources.length: One class period or more: mock scam video, reveal video, presentation, teacher's guide, worksheet and quiz
resources.summary: Students watch a fake but realistic investment promotion, then a video that takes it apart and shows the warning signs. Comes with a teacher's guide that assumes no background in investing — one of the best ready-made lessons on spotting investment fraud.

resources.title: Internet Crime Report 2025
resources.summary: The FBI's yearly breakdown of complaints and losses from online crime in the US, by crime type and victim age. The 2025 edition is the first to include a dedicated section on scams that use artificial intelligence. Useful raw material for data and media-literacy lessons. Keep in mind the figures come from complaints made to the FBI, not a survey of all crime.

resources.title: Consumer Sentinel Network Data Book (2024) and Explore Data dashboards
resources.length: Annual data book plus interactive dashboards updated quarterly
resources.summary: The FTC's data on millions of consumer reports about fraud, identity theft and other problems, with interactive dashboards by category, state and year. A ready-made source for classroom data projects on which scams are growing. The FTC notes the data comes from unverified consumer reports, not a survey.

resources.title: Pass It On
resources.type: Campaign materials (fact sheets, presentations, activity sheets)
resources.length: Short fact sheets, bookmarks, presentations and activity sheets
resources.licence: US federal government work; the FTC states all its information is in the public domain
resources.summary: Short, printable materials on impersonator, romance, grandkid, tech support, investment and 'you've won' scams, built around one idea: talk about scams with the people you know. Designed for older adults, but the one-page format works for any audience.

resources.title: FTC free consumer publications
resources.length: Dozens of leaflets and booklets on scams, privacy and credit
resources.licence: US federal government work; the FTC states its consumer education materials are free and in the public domain
resources.summary: The FTC's full catalogue of free consumer leaflets — scams, identity theft, privacy, credit and more. Each can be downloaded and printed, or ordered in bulk with free shipping within the US.

resources.title: The Little Book of Fraud
resources.summary: A widely used UK police guide to the most common scams — from bank impersonation and courier fraud to romance and investment scams — with plain advice on how to protect yourself and what to do if it happens. Adopted by police forces across the UK. Formerly published as 'The Little Book of Big Scams'.

resources.title: The Little Book of Cyber Scams 2.0
resources.publisher: Metropolitan Police Service Cyber Crime Unit (London, UK)
resources.summary: The online-focused companion to the Little Book of Fraud: phishing, hacking, ransomware and staying safe online, written for both individuals and small businesses.

resources.title: The Little Book of Scams
resources.publisher: Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) — National Anti-Scam Centre
resources.length: Short booklet, with an Easy Read version
resources.licence: Commonwealth of Australia copyright — link only
resources.summary: Australia's official guide to scams and the original that inspired the UK's Little Book of Fraud: the most common scams, how scammers make contact, the warning signs, and where to get help. The Easy Read version is especially useful for students and people with lower literacy. Formerly published as 'The Little Black Book of Scams'.

resources.title: A Guide to Scams (Easy Read)
resources.summary: An Easy Read, 44-page version of the National Anti-Scam Centre's guide to scams, using simple language and images to explain common scam warning signs and how to protect yourself, for readers who find standard text formats difficult to understand.

resources.title: How to Avoid a Scam
resources.summary: A downloadable FTC guide explaining practical ways to avoid scams, hosted on the agency's media library alongside its wider consumer-protection resources covering shopping, credit and debt, job offers, unwanted calls and messages, identity theft, and specific scam types such as romance and wire-transfer fraud.

resources.title: My Action Plan: How I'll Avoid a Scam
resources.language: English, Spanish, Vietnamese, Simplified Chinese and Korean
resources.summary: A fillable worksheet from the FTC's Consumer.gov that helps people decide in advance what they'll do if they get an unexpected call, text, email or social media message asking for money or personal information, available in English, Spanish, Vietnamese, Chinese and Korean.

resources.title: Scams and Identity Theft
resources.length: 6 resources (action plan worksheet, scam identification guide, identity theft protection, job scams, rental scams, post-scam response)
resources.language: English, Spanish, Vietnamese, Simplified Chinese and Korean
resources.summary: A Consumer.gov section of six guides and worksheets on recognising scam stories, protecting personal information, spotting fraudulent job and rental listings, and what to do after losing money to a scam, with separate materials for teachers and for service providers helping clients.

resources.title: Protecting Against and Recovering from Identity Theft and Scams
resources.summary: A 69-slide CFPB and FTC webinar deck from October 2021 on preventing and recovering from identity theft and scams, covering unwanted calls and texts, romance and online dating scams, and mortgage closing scams, with contact details for the CFPB's Office for Older Americans.

resources.title: How to Spot Frauds and Scams
resources.summary: A two-page CFPB guide listing common fraud tactics and their warning signs — promises of guaranteed riches, pressure to act immediately, claims of inside information, prize and lottery scams, and appeals to a shared community or special credentials — each paired with the underlying truth.

resources.title: Fraud Watch Network: handbooks and visual guides
resources.summary: A page from AARP, a US membership organisation for people 50 and older, compiling nine handbooks and visual guides on identifying scams, freezing credit, relationship fraud and seasonal scams, including a Watchdog Alert Handbook and a Visual Guide to Fraud.

resources.title: Scam Bingo Handbook
resources.type: Activity toolkit (posters, leaflets, Scam Bingo handbook and cards)
level: Organisations and businesses running awareness activities
resources.length: 11 downloadable resources (4 posters, 2 leaflets, 3 z-cards, 2 web banner sets, plus the Scam Bingo handbook and cards)
resources.language: English, with Scottish and Welsh versions for most resources
resources.licence: Not stated (page footer shows a standard © 2026 UK Finance notice)
resources.summary: A toolkit from Take Five, a fraud-awareness campaign led by UK Finance, a trade body representing UK banks, offering posters, leaflets and an interactive Scam Bingo handbook and cards for organisations to run fraud-prevention activities around the campaign's Stop, Challenge, Protect message.

resources.title: Golden Rules: Safe Online Shopping
resources.length: Not stated (part of a wider e-commerce fraud-prevention guide published 21 Jun 2017, updated 10 Feb 2025); available in around 29 country/language versions
resources.language: English, plus roughly 29 EU country/language versions
resources.licence: Not stated (page footer shows a standard © European Union Agency for Law Enforcement Cooperation notice)
resources.summary: Europol's 'Golden Rules' for safe online shopping, part of a wider e-commerce fraud guide: never send card details by email, be cautious with unfamiliar sites, use secure payment protocols and credit cards, and report fraud to your bank and police. Downloadable in around 29 languages.

resources.title: Online Fraud Schemes: A Web of Deceit
resources.length: Not stated (5 MB PDF; second in Europol's IOCTA 2023 Spotlight Report series)
resources.licence: Not stated (page footer shows a standard © European Union Agency for Law Enforcement Cooperation notice)
resources.summary: A Europol Spotlight Report, the second in the IOCTA 2023 series, examining online fraud schemes as a major EU crime threat generating billions in illicit profits yearly, covering the range of exclusively-online criminal activity that harms individuals, companies and public institutions.

resources.title: Consumer protection laws (Wex legal encyclopedia)
resources.publisher: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School
resources.length: Short encyclopedia entry with links to related terms
resources.summary: A clear starting point on how US consumer protection works: from 'let the buyer beware' to the FTC Act, the CFPB, specialised laws such as the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, and the state 'little FTC Acts'. Reviewed by Cornell's Wex team in September 2025.

resources.title: Business Law I Essentials (2nd edition)
resources.length: Full textbook with end-of-chapter questions and answer key
resources.summary: A short introductory textbook on US business law — the legal system, contracts, sales, torts — with a chapter on consumer protection covering unfair trade practices and the role of the FTC. Chapter 12, 'Unfair Trade Practices and the Federal Trade Commission,' covers consumer protection. Useful for understanding the legal framework behind everyday consumer disputes.

resources.title: Consumer Rights and Algorithms
resources.publisher: Gregory M. Dickinson — arXiv (open-access preprint, Computers and Society)
resources.summary: A 2026 overview of consumer protection law from its historical roots to the digital age: deception and unfair trade practices, how AI and big data are changing advertising and fraud, and regulatory responses such as data privacy laws and bans on dark patterns.

resources.title: Consumer Rights Act 2015 — Explanatory Notes
resources.length: Long document, organised by section of the Act
resources.licence: UK Open Government Licence / Crown copyright (link only)
resources.summary: The government's own plain-language explanation of the UK's main consumer law: rights when buying goods, digital content and services, the remedies when things go wrong, and unfair contract terms. Written for readers who are not lawyers. These notes explain the Act as passed in 2015; the Act itself has since been amended, so check the current version for anything recent.

resources.title: Business Companion — trading standards law explained
resources.publisher: Chartered Trading Standards Institute (CTSI), on behalf of the UK Department for Business and Trade
resources.length: Quick guides and in-depth guides on consumer protection law
resources.summary: Free, government-backed guidance on UK consumer law written by experts in trading standards: consumer contracts, returns, unfair terms, pricing and more. Written for businesses, which makes it a useful way for students to see consumer rights from the other side of the counter.

resources.title: Your rights when shopping in the EU
resources.summary: The EU's official explanation of the minimum two-year legal guarantee on goods, what you can ask for when something breaks (repair, replacement, price reduction or refund), and where to get help — with links to extra rights in each country.

resources.title: What are my consumer rights when shopping online?
resources.summary: A clear guide to online shopping rights in the EU, Norway and Iceland: the 14-day cooling-off period, refund deadlines, delivery within 30 days, and what to do if an order doesn't arrive. ECC-Net also helps consumers with cross-border disputes for free.

resources.title: Repair, replace, refund — consumer guarantees
resources.type: Official guidance and interactive problem solver
resources.length: Guidance pages plus an interactive problem solver
resources.summary: How Australia's consumer guarantees work: products must be safe, durable and as described, and when they aren't you're entitled to a repair, replacement or refund depending on whether the failure is major or minor. Includes an interactive problem solver to check your rights for a specific purchase.

resources.title: Consumer Law Essentials
resources.length: 7 chapters, plus a downloadable PDF and print-on-demand option
resources.summary: A collaborative, plain-language Clicklaw Wikibook from People's Law School, a British Columbia non-profit, explaining consumer rights when buying goods or hiring services, making contracts, preventing problems, and what to do if something goes wrong, downloadable as a PDF or ordered as a printed book.

resources.title: Consumer Law
resources.licence: CC licensed for sharing and re-use (specific CC variant not stated on this page); excerpts from the Restatements of the Law, Principles of the Law and the Model Penal Code are copyright The American Law Institute and reproduced by permission, outside the Creative Commons licence
resources.summary: An open, intentionally incomplete casebook on the H2O platform from Harvard's Library Innovation Lab, covering what consumer protection is for, fraud and deception, disclosure rules, unconscionability, product safety, equality and discrimination, and student debt, built from court cases, statutes and scholarly readings.

resources.title: Consumer Law module
resources.length: Not stated (semester-long module framework, taught Autumn 2009/10)
resources.summary: A university module framework on consumer protection law by Professor Peter Cartwright of the University of Nottingham, taught in Autumn 2009/10 to second and final-year undergraduates, viewable online or downloadable as a zip file, catalogued on MERLOT, a collaborative educational resource directory.

resources.title: Consumer Protection Manuals
resources.publisher: Idaho Office of the Attorney General
resources.length: 7 manuals (Consumer Protection Manual, Motor Vehicle Advertising Guidelines, Landlord and Tenant Guidelines, Lemon Law Manual, Older Adults Manual, Nonprofit Board Service, Young Adult Handbook)
resources.language: English, with Spanish versions of most manuals
resources.licence: Not stated (page footer shows a standard © 2026 Idaho Office of the Attorney General. All Rights Reserved. notice)
resources.summary: Seven manuals from the Idaho Attorney General's office covering consumer protection basics, motor vehicle advertising rules, landlord-tenant rights and responsibilities, the state's Lemon Law, consumer issues for older adults, nonprofit board service, and a handbook for young adults, most available in English and Spanish.

resources.title: Surveillance Self-Defense
resources.length: Dozens of guides: basics, step-by-step tool guides and scenario playlists
resources.summary: A practical, regularly updated guide to protecting your privacy online: making a security plan, passwords and two-factor authentication, avoiding phishing, phone privacy settings, and privacy when using AI tools. It includes a guide written specifically for students.

resources.title: Secure Our World
resources.publisher: Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), U.S. government
resources.length: Tip sheets, family guide, toolkit and activities such as bingo cards
resources.summary: The US government's ongoing online safety campaign, built around four habits: strong passwords and a password manager, multifactor authentication, recognising and reporting phishing, and keeping software updated. Includes printable tip sheets and simple classroom-friendly activities.

resources.title: Digital Literacy & Well-Being and Digital Citizenship curricula
resources.length: More than 140 lessons, plus AI literacy lessons
resources.licence: Free to use; lessons shareable with attribution for non-commercial use (link only). A free teacher account unlocks some materials.
resources.summary: Free, research-backed K–12 lessons on online privacy and safety, digital footprint, media literacy, cyberbullying and healthy tech habits, used in a large share of US schools. Each lesson comes with slides and activities.

resources.title: Libraries Stand for Privacy — Participant Handbook
resources.publisher: Sarah Hartman-Caverly (editor), Penn State University Libraries (Pressbooks)
resources.summary: A 2025 open handbook on privacy literacy written for libraries and educators, gathering key concepts and trusted tools for teaching people to protect their personal information.

resources.title: Cyber Aware
resources.length: Six key actions plus short guides
resources.summary: The UK government's top tips for staying secure online, built around six simple actions: a strong separate email password, passwords made of three random words, a password manager, 2-step verification, software updates and backups.

resources.title: Your data protection rights
resources.length: Guidance pages on each individual right
resources.summary: The UK data protection regulator's guidance for the public on your rights over your personal information — including how to ask an organisation for a copy of everything it holds about you (a subject access request), which in most cases is free and must be answered within one month.

resources.title: eSafety schools' hub
resources.length: Classroom resources, posters, videos with lesson plans, and free professional learning
resources.licence: Commonwealth of Australia copyright — link only
resources.summary: Australia's national online safety regulator gathers its school resources in one place: classroom lessons and videos with slide decks and worksheets, posters, an evidence-based framework for teaching online safety, and free training for teachers.

resources.title: Privacy Guides
resources.type: Reference site and handbook (tool recommendations, knowledge base)
resources.length: Not stated (ongoing knowledge base, tool recommendations, videos and news; no total count given)
resources.language: 10 languages (English, Spanish, French, Hebrew, Italian, Dutch, Russian, and two Chinese variants)
resources.licence: Not stated (page footer shows © 2021 Privacy Guides and contributors)
resources.summary: A non-profit, impartial site recommending privacy tools without affiliate bias, alongside a knowledge base, security news, educational videos, expert interviews and a weekly livestream, run by Privacy Guides to help people make informed privacy and security choices online.

resources.title: Security in-a-Box
resources.publisher: Tactical Tech and Front Line Defenders
resources.length: 24 guides across 6 topic areas (Assess & Plan, Passwords, Communication, Phones & Computers, Internet Connection, Files)
resources.language: 13 languages (Arabic, English, Spanish, Farsi, French, Indonesian, Burmese, Pashto, Portuguese, Russian, Turkish, Vietnamese, Simplified Chinese)
resources.summary: A digital security handbook from Tactical Tech and Front Line Defenders, organised into 24 guides across six areas — assessing risk, passwords, secure communication, protecting phones and computers, internet connections and files — available in 13 languages, with a companion blog on emerging security topics.

resources.title: Digital Citizenship Education Handbook
resources.length: 136 pages (2022 edition); a French edition was published in 2020
resources.language: English (2022 edition); French edition also available (2020)
resources.licence: Reproduction of extracts up to 500 words is authorised for non-commercial purposes, provided the text's integrity is preserved and the source is credited as ‘© Council of Europe, 2021’; other reproduction or translation requests go to the Directorate of Communications
resources.summary: The Council of Europe's handbook on digital citizenship, organised around being online, well-being online and rights online, with fact sheets on access, media literacy, ethics, health, e-presence and participation, including perspectives from children, teachers and parents on each topic.

resources.title: Personal Data and Privacy Protection in Online Learning
resources.publisher: UNESCO Institute for Information Technologies in Education (UNESCO IITE)
resources.language: English (a Russian version is also available)
resources.summary: A 2020 UNESCO IITE handbook guiding students, teachers and parents to protect personal data and privacy in online learning, covering risks and strategies before, during and after learning, developed by Beijing Normal University's Smart Learning Institute alongside a related technical guide for education platforms.

resources.title: Guía de Privacidad y Seguridad en Internet
resources.publisher: Agencia Española de Protección de Datos (AEPD) and Instituto Nacional de Ciberseguridad (INCIBE), via Consumo Responde
resources.length: 18 fact sheets (fichas), each covering one risk and its safeguards
resources.summary: A Spanish-language guide jointly published by Spain's data protection agency (AEPD) and national cybersecurity institute (INCIBE), made up of 18 fact sheets on risks like weak passwords, phishing, cloud and social media privacy, parental mediation and online shopping, each paired with practical safeguards.

resources.title: Protecting Your Privacy and Security
resources.publisher: Internet Society — Online Trust and Safety Hub
resources.length: 5 sections (Understand; Secure Your Accounts and Devices; Control What You Share; Communicate Privately and Browse Safely; Respond and Report), plus a 'Five Things to Do Today' quick-start list
resources.summary: A non-technical guide from the Internet Society's Online Trust and Safety Hub on protecting an email account first, turning on automatic updates, limiting location sharing, using encrypted messaging, and checking app permissions, plus deeper sections on securing accounts, controlling sharing, and responding to incidents.

resources.title: Health Policy 101
resources.publisher: KFF (non-profit health policy research organisation), edited by Drew Altman
resources.length: 16 chapters, each downloadable as a PDF and updated regularly
resources.licence: Free to read and download for students and faculty (link only)
resources.summary: A free 'mini textbook' on US health policy written for students and faculty: Medicare, Medicaid, the Affordable Care Act, employer insurance, health care costs and affordability, medical debt, the regulation of private insurance, and an international comparison of health systems.

resources.title: Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms
resources.publisher: HealthCare.gov (U.S. Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services)
resources.length: Glossary page with a downloadable PDF and a worked example
resources.summary: The official US definitions of the words that make health insurance confusing — deductible, coinsurance, copayment, out-of-pocket limit — with an illustrated example of how they work together when you actually get care.

resources.title: Medical bill rights — consumer guides
resources.publisher: U.S. Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS)
resources.summary: Plain-language fact sheets on your rights against surprise medical bills under the No Surprises Act: what a surprise bill is, what a good faith estimate is, how to read a medical bill and how it differs from an Explanation of Benefits, and what to know before signing a consent form.

resources.title: No Surprises Act — Consumer Advocate Toolkit
resources.publisher: U.S. Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS)
resources.length: Toolkit with decision trees, sample documents and key terms
resources.summary: A deeper guide to the federal surprise-billing protections, built for people who help others with medical bills. Includes decision trees showing when the protections apply, a sample good faith estimate and a sample notice — useful for case-study work in class.

resources.title: Mirror, Mirror 2024: A Portrait of the Failing U.S. Health System — Comparing Performance in 10 Nations
resources.publisher: The Commonwealth Fund (private foundation) — David Blumenthal et al.
resources.summary: Compares the health systems of 10 high-income countries, including the US, UK, Germany and Australia, on 70 measures of access, care process, administrative efficiency, equity and outcomes. A good basis for discussing how rankings are built: the result depends on which measures are chosen and how they are weighted.

resources.title: Health at a Glance 2025: OECD Indicators
resources.length: About 244 pages, readable online or as a PDF
resources.summary: The standard international reference for comparing health systems: life expectancy, access and quality of care, waiting times, and how much each country spends on health and how that spending is financed. Built from comparable official national statistics.

resources.title: Medical Debt Manual
resources.summary: A New Jersey-specific manual helping insured and uninsured consumers understand their rights on the cost of medical care, covering plan types, options for the uninsured like FQHCs and charity care, reading and disputing bills, and protections against aggressive debt collection, in English and Spanish.

resources.title: FAIR Health Consumer
resources.type: Consumer education site and cost-estimator tools
resources.length: Not stated (ongoing site: cost tools, articles, glossary; no total count given)
resources.language: English (Spanish version noted: FAIR Health Consumidor)
resources.licence: Not stated (page footer shows © 2026 FAIR Health, Inc.)
resources.summary: FAIR Health, an independent national nonprofit, estimates healthcare and dental costs for thousands of procedures using tens of billions of real insurance claim records, and offers tools for older adults, shared decision-making, insurance basics articles and a glossary to help consumers plan for medical expenses.

resources.title: Medical bill guides and resources
resources.length: 4 sections linking to further guides (Toolkit for patient advocates; Understanding your healthcare; Checking and disputing a bill; Getting support)
resources.language: English (phone support available in Spanish, French and 350+ other languages)
resources.summary: A CMS hub of guides for navigating medical billing issues: a No Surprises Act toolkit for patient advocates, how to read a bill or an explanation of benefits, types of health insurance, good faith estimates, disputing errors, appealing a plan decision, and finding financial assistance.

resources.title: Health insurance terms you should know
resources.length: Not stated (alphabetical glossary of billing terms)
resources.summary: A CMS glossary of medical billing terms tied to the No Surprises Act, explaining allowed amount, balance billing, coinsurance, copayment and cost sharing with worked dollar examples, plus how to file a complaint if a provider or plan breaks the billing protection rules.

resources.title: What should I do if I can't pay a medical bill?
resources.summary: CFPB guidance on what to do if you can't pay a medical bill: verify the debt and check for errors, explore insurance appeals and No Surprises Act protections, look into nonprofit hospital charity care, and negotiate a payment plan instead of using a credit card.

resources.title: HealthCare.gov glossary
resources.language: English (Spanish translation available; additional languages listed)
resources.summary: HealthCare.gov's general glossary defines over 350 terms used in the Health Insurance Marketplace, covering coverage types, government programs like Medicare, Medicaid and CHIP, plan categories such as Bronze and Gold, and cost-sharing concepts, distinct from the site's own separate SBC glossary.

resources.title: Dollar For: guides to hospital bill forgiveness
resources.length: 6-step guide, each step linking to a deeper how-to page
resources.summary: Dollar For, a nonprofit, publishes a free six-step do-it-yourself handbook for applying for hospital financial assistance: checking eligibility, filling out and submitting the application, following up, celebrating or appealing the decision, and other ways to lower a bill, with deeper how-to guides at each step.

resources.title: Family Voices resources
resources.type: Resource library (webinar archives, tip sheets, best practices)
level: Families of children and youth with special health care needs or disabilities
resources.licence: Not stated (page footer shows Copyright © 2025 Family Voices)
resources.summary: A searchable library of free resources (webinar archives, tip sheets and best practices) in English, Spanish, Chinese and Vietnamese, from Family Voices, a family-led organization that transforms systems of care for children and youth, especially those with special health care needs or disabilities.

resources.title: Triage Cancer resources
resources.language: English and Spanish, plus some resources in other languages
resources.summary: Triage Cancer's free resources — animated videos, Quick Guides and Checklists, and state law summaries — cover health insurance, Medicare, Medicaid, appeals, disability insurance, work, finances, estate planning and legal issues, for individuals diagnosed with cancer, their caregivers, and health care professionals, including Spanish-language materials.

resources.title: Renters' Rights Act overview for tenants
resources.licence: UK Open Government Licence / Crown copyright (link only)
resources.summary: The official summary of how private renting in England changed on 1 May 2026: most tenancies became rolling (periodic) with no fixed end date, rent can only be increased through a formal yearly process, and tenants can end a tenancy with two months' notice. Applies to England only.

resources.title: Renters' Rights Act: private tenants
resources.summary: Independent, practical advice from England's best-known housing charity on what the Renters' Rights Act means for private tenants: the end of section 21 and fixed-term tenancies, rent increase rules, the right to ask to keep a pet, and the 1-month limit on rent in advance.

resources.title: Your Home Loan Toolkit: A step-by-step guide
resources.summary: The booklet US lenders must give every home buyer, written in plain language: how much you can afford, how your credit affects your interest rate, how to compare loan offers, and how to read your Loan Estimate and Closing Disclosure.

resources.title: Report Housing Discrimination
resources.publisher: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)
resources.summary: How to report housing discrimination to HUD's Fair Housing and Equal Opportunity office: what counts as a violation under the Fair Housing Act and the Violence Against Women Act, and how to file a complaint online, by phone, or by mail.

resources.title: Out of Reach 2026: The High Cost of Housing
resources.publisher: National Low Income Housing Coalition (NLIHC, non-profit)
resources.length: Full report plus interactive data for every state, metro area and county
resources.summary: Calculates the 'Housing Wage' — the hourly wage a full-time worker needs to rent a modest home without spending more than 30% of income on rent — for every US state and county. Strong material for data lessons, and for debate: the report is produced by an advocacy group, and critics argue the fixed 30% benchmark overstates how unaffordable housing is.

resources.title: Tenants' Rights Handbook
resources.publisher: Texas Young Lawyers Association and the State Bar of Texas
resources.licence: May be republished with attribution to the Texas Young Lawyers Association (per tyla.org); the PDF itself carries no further licence terms, just copyright years 1985-2019
resources.summary: A 43-page handbook for Texas residential tenants, produced by the Texas Young Lawyers Association and the State Bar of Texas, explaining common landlord-tenant legal issues under the Texas Property Code, intended as general guidance rather than a substitute for legal advice.

resources.title: Tenants' Rights Handbook (Spanish edition)
resources.publisher: Texas Young Lawyers Association and the State Bar of Texas
resources.licence: May be republished with attribution to the Texas Young Lawyers Association (per tyla.org); the PDF itself carries no further licence terms, just copyright years 1985-2019
resources.summary: The Spanish-language edition of the Texas Young Lawyers Association and State Bar of Texas handbook for Texas residential tenants, covering the same landlord-tenant legal issues under the Texas Property Code as the English edition, produced as a public service for Spanish-speaking tenants.

resources.title: Housing self-help guides (Know Your Rights series)
resources.publisher: Legal Aid of Western Ohio, Inc.
resources.length: ~20 materials: rent escrow guides, security deposit guides, a Know Your Rights booklet plus 11 flyers, and 3 interactive self-help forms
resources.licence: Not stated (page footer shows © 2026 Legal Aid of Western Ohio, Inc.)
resources.summary: Downloadable Ohio tenant self-help materials from Legal Aid of Western Ohio: rent escrow brochures, a security deposit packet, a Know Your Rights booklet and flyers on repairs, utility shut-offs and lease signing, plus online tools to prepare an eviction answer or a poverty affidavit.

resources.title: Tenants' Rights
resources.publisher: Pennsylvania Legal Aid Network, via PALawHelp.org (a project of the Pennsylvania Legal Aid Network and the Legal Services Corporation)
resources.length: 91 resources across legal information, notice requirements, hearing/appeal procedure, self-help forms, and county-specific materials
resources.licence: Not stated (page footer shows a general © Scale Justice copyright notice for the site platform)
resources.summary: A Pennsylvania-specific directory of 91 tenants' rights resources from PALawHelp.org, a project of the Pennsylvania Legal Aid Network and the Legal Services Corporation, covering legal information, notice requirements, hearing and appeal procedures, self-help forms, and county-specific guidance across the state.

resources.title: Juventud con derechos: guía de los derechos de las inquilinas
resources.publisher: Ministerio de Juventud e Infancia (Gobierno de España), a través del Instituto de la Juventud (INJUVE)
resources.summary: A free 2025 Spanish-language guide on tenants' rights for young people, published by Spain's Ministry of Youth and Childhood through the Youth Institute (INJUVE). Despite its general 'Youth with Rights' title, this edition is specifically about housing law and renters' rights, not a broader guide.

resources.title: Free Credit Reports
resources.summary: How to get your credit reports for free from the one official site, AnnualCreditReport.com — now available every week from all three national credit bureaus — and how to spot the look-alike sites that charge you or steal your details. Note that the free reports don't include a credit score.

resources.title: Loan Simulator
resources.publisher: Federal Student Aid, U.S. Department of Education
resources.summary: The official tool for estimating federal student loan payments: compare repayment plans, see the effect of borrowing more, or explore options if payments become hard to manage. Students planning to borrow can use it before taking out any loan.

resources.title: Using a student loan calculator — classroom activity
resources.length: One class period: teacher guide and student worksheet
resources.summary: A ready-to-teach activity in which students use the official federal Loan Simulator to see how much a student loan really costs over time, and learn the difference between federal and private student loans. Pairs directly with the Loan Simulator listed in this section.

resources.title: MoneyHelper
resources.length: Guides, budget planner, calculators and a free debt advice locator
resources.summary: The UK's free, impartial, government-backed money guidance service: what to know before you borrow, how credit ratings work, how to prioritise several debts, and a tool to find free accredited debt advice nearby.

resources.title: Moneysmart — credit and loans
resources.summary: Australia's official free money guidance from the financial regulator, including how credit cards, personal loans and buy-now-pay-later work, how to check your credit report, and calculators to see the real cost of borrowing.

resources.title: Credit reports and scores
resources.length: Hub page linking to basics, key terms, common issues, rights and how-to guides
resources.summary: A CFPB hub on credit reports and scores covering how to request your reports, the difference between a report and a score, common issues like denied credit or identity theft, your rights, a list of credit reporting companies, and how-to guides for disputing errors.

resources.title: Know your rights when a debt collector calls
resources.length: Single article, printable as a handout
resources.summary: CFPB guidance on confronting a debt collector directly: verify who's calling, ask for the amount owed and proof the debt is yours, know your right to dispute or stop contact, keep records, and understand what debt collectors are legally barred from doing under the FDCPA.

resources.title: Payday loans: consumer guide
resources.length: Hub page linking to basics, key terms, common issues, rights and how-to guides
resources.summary: A CFPB hub explaining payday loans: common characteristics, how to decide if one is your best option, typical costs and fees, your rights such as protection from wage garnishment without a court order, and how-to guides for comparing costs using APR.

resources.title: Debt Collection FAQs
resources.length: Single long-form FAQ article in 5 sections
resources.summary: FTC answers to frequently asked questions about debt collection under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act: what debts are covered, when and how collectors can contact you, what they must disclose, disputing a debt, lawsuits and garnishment, and time-barred old debts.

resources.title: What to know about payday and car title loans
resources.summary: An FTC guide to payday and car title loans: typical fees and APRs (around 391% for payday loans, 300% for title loans), how rollovers increase costs, the risk of vehicle repossession, cheaper alternatives like credit union PAL loans, and protections for servicemembers.

resources.title: Managing My Money for Young Adults: Borrowing
resources.length: Session 6 of an 8-session, 24-hour course (1-2 hours for this session)
resources.summary: Session 6, 'Understanding debt and how to borrow wisely', from the Open University's free course for young adults: who you can borrow from, when borrowing is sensible versus reckless, what determines the cost of borrowing, and how different debt products rank by interest rate charged.

resources.title: Free financial education guides and downloads
resources.length: ~23 guide topics (most with full and short versions, many in English and Spanish) plus 5 financial worksheets
resources.summary: Credit.org, an independent 501(c)(3) nonprofit financial counseling agency, offers free downloadable guides and worksheets on debt, credit, budgeting, identity theft, predatory lending, job loss, homeownership and more, plus worksheets for budgeting, tracking debt, and calculating net worth.

resources.title: Credit and debt fact sheets
resources.length: 3 PDF fact sheets: Budget sheet, Help with debt, Sample debt letters
resources.licence: Not stated (page footer shows © 2026 Citizens Advice. All rights reserved.)
resources.summary: Three downloadable PDF fact sheets from Citizens Advice Scotland: a budget sheet, a 'help with debt' guide, and sample debt letters you can use when writing to creditors, with separate versions of this page available for England, Northern Ireland and Wales.

resources.title: Student debt advice guide
resources.summary: A 23-page free guide from StepChange Debt Charity helping students organise their money, increase income, understand available funding, manage borrowing sensibly, find advice, and know what to do if worried about debts, covering budgeting, student bank accounts and cutting everyday spending.

resources.title: Credit card debt: what to do if you cannot pay
resources.length: Single article covering 5 impacts of credit card debt
resources.summary: StepChange Debt Charity explains how credit card debt escalates through high interest rates, outlines what 'persistent debt' means after 18 months of minimum payments, and describes the knock-on effects: a damaged credit file, difficulty getting new credit, and the toll on mental health.

resources.title: Mental Health & Debt (44-page booklet)
resources.summary: A free 44-page MoneySavingExpert booklet by Martin Lewis and Jenny Keefe, supported by Mind, Rethink and CAP, covering debt crisis versus worrying debts, finding free debt counselling, working with banks about a condition, coping approaches, and how friends and family can help.

resources.title: Using credit wisely
resources.length: 4 sections: using credit for essentials, managing repayments, borrowing from family, lending to family or friends
resources.licence: Not stated (© 2026 Money and Pensions Service. All rights reserved.)
resources.summary: MoneyHelper's guide to using credit without falling into debt, for people overloaded with credit cards, loans, overdrafts or Buy Now Pay Later, covering reviewing your budget, using savings to pay off credit, avoiding cash withdrawals on cards, and the risks of borrowing from family.

resources.title: Help if you are struggling to clear credit card debt
resources.licence: Not stated (© 2026 Money and Pensions Service. All rights reserved.)
resources.summary: MoneyHelper explains 'persistent debt' (paying more in interest and fees than you've repaid over 18 months), what your credit card provider must do about it, how minimum repayments work, options like balance transfers, and what happens if you ignore the provider's contact.

resources.title: YouthRules! Young Worker Toolkit
resources.publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
resources.length: Collection of fact sheets, calendars and guides
resources.summary: The US government's resources on the rules for working teenagers: which jobs under-18s can and can't do, how many hours 14- and 15-year-olds can work on school days and school weeks, plus calendars to track your own hours and understand overtime. Note that each state also has its own rules, and the stricter one applies.

resources.title: Youth@Work
resources.summary: The EEOC's programme to teach young workers about their rights against discrimination and harassment at work: what counts as illegal discrimination, how to respond if it happens to you or a co-worker, and classroom guides for teachers.

resources.title: Young workers and students
resources.length: Guidance pages plus pay, shift and leave calculators
resources.summary: Australia's workplace regulator explains what young workers and students are entitled to — the minimum working age, getting ready for your first day, pay and conditions, and workplace bullying, harassment and discrimination — and offers a free Pay Calculator to check you're being paid correctly.

resources.title: Understanding Rights at Work: A Guide to Key Terms Related to Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work
level: International — governments, employers' and workers' organizations, businesses, researchers
resources.language: English (also available in Spanish and French)
resources.summary: An International Labour Organization guide defining key terms in fundamental principles and rights at work, trade and supply chains, covering forced labour, child labour, collective bargaining, equality, non-discrimination and occupational safety, developed for an international audience of governments, employers, workers and researchers.

resources.title: Workers' Rights
resources.licence: Public domain — material may be reproduced, fully or partially, without permission; source credit requested but not required
resources.summary: A 28-page United States OSHA booklet summarising worker rights under the Occupational Safety and Health Act: filing a confidential inspection complaint, getting training you understand, reviewing injury and illness records, participating in inspections, and filing a retaliation complaint if an employer punishes you.

resources.title: Whistleblower protection resources
resources.publisher: OSHA (US Department of Labor) — Whistleblower Protection Program
resources.length: Hub page linking to retaliation guidance, complaint filing, and anti-retaliation program resources
resources.summary: The United States Whistleblower Protection Program, run by OSHA, explains what counts as retaliation, how to file a retaliation complaint, protections by subject, how to build an anti-retaliation program, and how to file a safety and health complaint.

resources.title: Resources for Workers (workers' rights materials in multiple languages)
resources.publisher: US Department of Labor — Wage and Hour Division
resources.length: Hub page linking to dozens of materials in 20+ languages
resources.language: English, Spanish, Chinese, Korean, Polish, Tagalog, Thai, Russian, Vietnamese, Haitian Creole, Somali, Nepalese and others
resources.summary: The US Department of Labor's Wage and Hour Division offers worker rights materials in 20+ languages, including complaint cards, industry-specific rights cards for farm, nail salon, health care, H-1B and H-2A workers, workplace posters, fact sheets, and a Did You Know? booklet.

resources.title: Key Employment Rights
resources.licence: Open Parliament Licence (© House of Commons 2026)
resources.summary: A United Kingdom House of Commons Library briefing on key statutory employment rights in Great Britain: unfair dismissal, deduction from wages, and working time limits and rest breaks, plus shorter coverage of agency workers, equality and discrimination, redundancy, the National Minimum Wage, and whistleblowing.

resources.title: Employment Rights Act 2025: factsheets
resources.publisher: UK Government — Department for Business and Trade
resources.summary: 24 UK government factsheets on the Employment Rights Act 2025, covering statutory sick pay, zero hours contracts, fire and rehire, flexible working, whistleblower protections, trade unions and unfair dismissal, published by the Department for Business and Trade to help employees and employers understand the Act.

resources.title: Advice (employment rights guidance)
resources.length: 6 topic sections plus templates and Codes of Practice
resources.summary: Acas, the UK's independent workplace advice body, provides free employment guidance for England, Scotland and Wales, organised into pay and hours, holiday and leave, equality and wellbeing, starting and ending employment, consultation and change, and conflict and resolution, alongside templates and statutory Codes of Practice.

resources.title: Rights at work
resources.publisher: European Commission — Employment, Social Affairs and Inclusion
resources.summary: The European Commission outlines every EU worker's minimum rights: health and safety at work, equal opportunities for women and men, protection against discrimination on sex, race, religion, age, disability or sexual orientation, and labour law covering part-time work, fixed-term contracts and working hours.

resources.title: An employee's guide to fixing workplace problems
resources.summary: A 14-page Australian Fair Work Ombudsman guide walking employees through a four-step process for fixing a workplace problem: check your legal entitlements, talk to your boss, put your concerns in writing, and take further action through a union, the Ombudsman or the Fair Work Commission.

resources.title: Your guide to casual employment
resources.summary: A 13-page Australian Fair Work Ombudsman guide to casual employment: how casual employees differ from permanent employees, casual loading (typically an extra 25% of the minimum hourly rate), entitlements like unpaid carer's and compassionate leave, and the 'employee choice pathway' for becoming a permanent employee.

resources.title: A guide to starting a new job
resources.summary: A 10-page Australian Fair Work Ombudsman guide for employees starting a new job, listing what to find out from your employer before day one (pay rate, hours, award coverage, probation), a first-day checklist, and what leave entitlements apply, such as annual, sick and carer's leave.

resources.title: Airline refunds: when you're entitled to one
resources.publisher: U.S. Department of Transportation — Aviation Consumer Protection
resources.summary: When US rules entitle you to a refund from an airline: a cancelled flight, a significant delay or schedule change you don't accept, delayed bags or extra services you paid for and didn't get — plus the 24-hour rule for cancelling a booking without penalty.

resources.title: Airline Cancellation and Delay Dashboard
resources.summary: Shows, airline by airline, what each US carrier has committed to provide when a delay or cancellation is its own fault — meals, hotels, rebooking, compensation. These are the airlines' own commitments, which DOT can hold them to, and they can change over time.

resources.title: Air passenger rights in the EU
resources.summary: The EU's official explanation of your rights when a flight departing from the EU (or arriving with an EU airline) is delayed, cancelled or overbooked: assistance, rerouting or refund, and when compensation is due. As of this check, the page still describes the existing Regulation 261/2004 framework and does not yet reflect the revised regulation the European Parliament approved in July 2026 — worth re-checking as that reform is implemented.

resources.title: Flight delays and cancellations — your rights
resources.summary: The UK aviation regulator's guidance on what airlines owe you when a flight from the UK is delayed or cancelled, how to claim, and where to go if the airline says no. Covers delays, cancellations, denied boarding, missed flights, downgrading and how to make a compensation claim.

resources.title: Buying a used car from a dealer
resources.summary: What to check before buying a used car in the US, including the Buyers Guide that dealers must display on every used car: whether it's sold 'as is' or with a warranty, why spoken promises are hard to enforce, and why to get the car inspected by an independent mechanic before you buy.

resources.title: Check for vehicle safety recalls
resources.summary: The official US tool for checking whether a car has an unrepaired safety recall, using its vehicle identification number (VIN). A simple, practical step before buying any used car.

resources.title: Passenger rights
resources.length: Hub page linking to air, rail, bus/coach and ship passenger rights pages
resources.language: English (also available in other EU languages)
resources.summary: European Union passenger rights for air, rail, bus and coach, and ship travel: delays and cancellations, where you have rights when travelling, and a free 'Your Passenger Rights' smartphone app, with links to mode-specific pages covering air, rail, bus and coach, and ship passenger rights.

resources.title: National enforcement bodies (NEB)
resources.length: Hub page linking to NEB documents for air, road, rail and maritime transport
resources.summary: The European Union's hub listing the national enforcement bodies (NEBs) that each EU member state must set up to monitor compliance with passenger rights rules and handle complaints, with separate regulatory documents for air, road (bus and coach), rail, and maritime transport across member states.

resources.title: Rights for travellers with disabilities or reduced mobility
level: Travellers with disabilities or reduced mobility
resources.length: Single overview page plus FAQs and mode-specific pages
resources.language: English (also available in other EU languages)
resources.summary: European Union passenger rights for travellers with disabilities or reduced mobility: accessible travel information, free assistance at terminals and on board for air, rail, bus/coach and ship journeys, and protection against being refused transport because of a disability, with links to the underlying EU regulations.

resources.title: Aviation Consumer Protection
resources.length: Hub page linking to topic-specific guidance
resources.summary: The United States Department of Transportation's Office of Aviation Consumer Protection hub on air passenger rights: flight delays and cancellations, bumping and oversales, tarmac delays, lost or damaged baggage, discrimination, refunds, buying a ticket, family seating, and how to file a consumer complaint.

resources.title: Air Travel Consumer Reports
resources.summary: Monthly United States data reports from the Department of Transportation's Office of Aviation Consumer Protection on airline service quality: flight delays, mishandled baggage and wheelchairs, oversales, consumer complaints, and animal incidents, drawing on Bureau of Transportation Statistics and TSA customer service data.

resources.title: Airline Passengers with Disabilities Bill of Rights
resources.summary: The United States Department of Transportation's Bill of Rights summarising the ten fundamental rights of air travelers with disabilities under the Air Carrier Access Act: dignity and respect, accessible information, airport and aircraft assistance, assistive devices and service animals, seating accommodations, and complaint resolution.

resources.title: Travel delays and cancellations
resources.summary: The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission explains consumer guarantee rights when a travel service is delayed or cancelled: a replacement or refund if not resolved within a reasonable time, how airline compensation policies work alongside consumer guarantees, and what steps to take next.

resources.title: Flights, cancellations and delays
resources.length: Single guide page with a 4-step complaint process
resources.summary: New Zealand's Consumer Protection agency explains your rights when a flight is cancelled, delayed or overbooked under the Consumer Guarantees Act and Fair Trading Act: refunds, rebooking, reimbursement or compensation depending on whether the airline or an outside cause was responsible, plus a complaint guide.

resources.title: Travel Rights
resources.length: 5 topic sections (flights, package holidays, hotels/accommodation, train delays, car hire)
resources.summary: Which?, a United Kingdom consumer organisation, provides a travel rights library covering flights (claiming compensation for delays or cancellations), package holidays, hotels and accommodation complaints, train delay compensation, and car hire disputes, with practical guides and free letter templates for each topic.

resources.title: Avoid Scams When You Travel
resources.summary: The United States FTC warns about common travel scams: fake free-vacation offers, illegal robocalls, copycat visa and passport sites, fake international driving permits, hijacked vacation rental listings, and unauthorised charter flights, with signs to watch for and tips to avoid being scammed before you book.

resources.title: Timeshares, Vacation Clubs, and Related Scams
resources.summary: The United States FTC explains timeshares and vacation clubs, how to handle high-pressure sales presentations, what to know before committing, and how to spot timeshare resale and exit scams where companies charge upfront fees and falsely guarantee a quick sale or big returns.

resources.title: Bringing Dark Patterns to Light
resources.length: Full report with an appendix cataloguing common dark patterns
resources.summary: The FTC's 2022 report on 'dark patterns' — website and app designs that push people into choices they didn't intend, such as hidden fees, pre-ticked boxes and subscriptions that are hard to cancel. Its appendix is a ready-made catalogue for a lesson on spotting manipulative design. Note that it predates later developments: the FTC's 2024 'click-to-cancel' rule was struck down by a federal appeals court in 2025.

resources.title: Online Choice Architecture: How digital design can harm competition and consumers
resources.length: Discussion paper (about 76 pages) plus a separate evidence review
resources.licence: UK Open Government Licence / Crown copyright (link only)
resources.summary: A clear framework from the UK competition regulator for understanding how online design shapes what we buy: defaults, rankings, false scarcity ('only 2 left!'), drip pricing and more, with real case studies. The companion evidence review summarises the research behind 21 of these practices — useful for university work.

resources.title: Dark Commercial Patterns
resources.summary: An international review of dark patterns in online commerce: a working definition, a taxonomy, the evidence on how much they influence consumer decisions, and how different countries are responding.

resources.title: Guidelines 03/2022 on deceptive design patterns in social media platform interfaces
resources.summary: The EU data protection regulators' guidance on design tricks in social media apps that nudge users into sharing more personal data than they intended, organised around the stages of using a platform, from signing up to deleting an account, with examples of each. This is the final adopted version (2.0).

resources.title: Free trials, automatic renewals and cancelling subscriptions
resources.summary: The FTC's plain-language advice on 'free' trials that turn into paid subscriptions, automatic renewals, and what to do if a company makes it hard to cancel or keeps charging you.

resources.title: Online Shopping
resources.summary: The US Federal Trade Commission's guide to shopping safely online: researching sellers and reading reviews critically, comparison shopping, checking delivery and refund policies, paying by credit card for dispute protection, keeping purchase records, and understanding what personal data shopping apps and sites collect.

resources.title: Solving Problems With a Business: Returns, Refunds, and Other Resolutions
resources.length: Single article, 5 sections plus sample complaint letter
resources.summary: The US Federal Trade Commission's guide to resolving problems with a business: returning items within deadlines, writing an effective complaint letter, getting help from attorneys general, consumer groups or the Better Business Bureau, posting honest online reviews, and using mediation, arbitration or small claims court.

resources.title: How To Evaluate Online Reviews
resources.summary: The US Federal Trade Commission explains how to spot fake or manipulated online reviews: checking a reviewer's history, watching for sudden bursts of reviews, noticing incentive disclosure badges, and remembering that fake reviews can be negative as well as positive, aimed at harming competitors.

resources.title: Unfair commercial practices
resources.language: English (also available in other EU languages)
resources.summary: Your Europe, the European Commission's citizen portal, lists commercial practices banned across the EU as unfair or aggressive, including dark design patterns, fake consumer reviews, bait advertising and pressure selling, and explains how to report or complain about such practices.

resources.title: Protecting you when buying online
resources.language: English (also available in other EU languages)
resources.summary: The European Commission explains EU e-commerce consumer rights: a two-year legal guarantee on goods, a 14-day right to cancel online orders, guaranteed delivery deadlines, bans on misleading urgency tactics, plus security tips for safe online payments and tools like the Safety Gate product alert system.

resources.title: 2022 – sweep on dark patterns
resources.summary: The European Commission's 2022 sweep on dark patterns screened 399 websites across 23 EU Member States plus Norway and Iceland for fake countdown timers, false hierarchy and hidden information, finding issues on 148 sites, and concluding over 37% potentially breach EU consumer law.

resources.title: Consumer rights and guarantees
resources.summary: The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission explains the nine consumer guarantees for products and three for services that apply automatically under Australian law, when exceptions apply, and what remedies — repair, replacement or refund — consumers can expect, with versions available in multiple languages.

resources.title: Cancelling a service you've arranged
resources.licence: © Citizens Advice. All rights reserved. (link only)
resources.summary: Citizens Advice explains UK consumer cancellation rights for services arranged online, by phone or mail order: a 14-day cooling-off period to cancel for any reason and get a refund, when that period does not apply, and how to negotiate charges or use alternative dispute resolution.

resources.title: Recognising ads: Social media and influencer marketing
resources.summary: The Advertising Standards Authority and CAP explain UK rules for influencer marketing on social media: when a post must be labelled as advertising, how prominent and clear labels like 'Ad' should be, and why terms such as 'sponsored' or 'gifted' are not sufficient disclosure.

resources.title: ICPEN Dark Patterns in Subscription Services Sweep Public Report
resources.publisher: International Consumer Protection and Enforcement Network (ICPEN)
resources.summary: ICPEN's 2024 international sweep by 27 consumer protection agencies in 26 countries examined 642 traders' subscription services and found 75.7% used at least one dark pattern, detailing sneaking, interface interference, obstruction, social proof, forced action, urgency and nagging practices that manipulate consumers.

resources.title: Complaints about a university or college
resources.summary: The Office for Students explains the complaint pathway for English higher education students: raise it with your university or college first, then escalate unresolved problems to the Office of the Independent Adjudicator, and how to notify the OfS if a provider is failing its duties.

resources.title: Course, campus or university closures
resources.length: Overview page linking to 3 further sections
resources.summary: The Office for Students explains students' rights in England if their course, campus or university closes, including student protection plans that universities must have, and points to further guidance on what to expect from your institution and support available for affected students.

resources.title: What you can expect from your university or college
resources.summary: The Office for Students sets out what English higher education students should expect during a closure: reading your university's student protection plan, understanding options like credit transfer and refunds, and knowing you're still entitled to the level of service promised in your student contract.

resources.title: Good Practice Framework: Handling complaints and academic appeals
resources.publisher: Office of the Independent Adjudicator for Higher Education (OIA)
resources.length: Guidance document, PDF 405KB (also available in Welsh)
resources.licence: © 2026 Office of the Independent Adjudicator for Higher Education (link only)
resources.summary: The OIA's Good Practice Framework guides higher education providers in England and Wales on handling student complaints and academic appeals fairly, covering timeframes, record-keeping and group complaints; it is also a useful resource for students and those who advise them.

resources.title: Student finance: how you're assessed and paid 2026 to 2027
resources.summary: Student Finance England explains how undergraduate finance applications are assessed and paid for students in England studying anywhere in the UK: eligibility, household income assessment for Maintenance Loans and Grants, and payment timing, with tuition fees paid directly to the university in instalments.

resources.title: Your guide to Student Finance England
resources.summary: Student Finance England's plain-language guide for students in England covers Tuition Fee Loans, Maintenance Loans, Disabled Students' Allowance and other grants, how household income is assessed, the application journey from applying to repayment, and what you'll need to apply for student finance.

resources.title: An Eligible Student Guide to the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA)
resources.publisher: US Department of Education (Student Privacy Policy Office)
level: Eligible students, 18+ or in postsecondary education (United States)
resources.summary: The US Department of Education explains FERPA rights that transfer to students once they turn 18 or enter postsecondary education: the right to inspect and review education records within 45 days, to request corrections, and to control third-party disclosure of personally identifiable information.

resources.title: An Eligible Student Guide to the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) (En Español)
resources.publisher: US Department of Education (Student Privacy Policy Office)
