level: Eligible students, 18+ or in postsecondary education (United States)
resources.summary: The US Department of Education's Spanish-language translation of its FERPA guide for eligible students: explaining that rights transfer from parents when a student turns 18 or enters postsecondary education, covering access to records, corrections, and consent before third parties see personal education information.

resources.title: Disability Discrimination: Academic Adjustments for Postsecondary Students
resources.publisher: US Department of Education (Office for Civil Rights)
level: Students with disabilities in postsecondary education (United States)
resources.length: Guidance hub page with linked policy documents
resources.summary: The US Department of Education's Office for Civil Rights explains academic adjustments available to postsecondary students with disabilities: modifications like priority registration, reduced course load, note takers and extended testing time, how to request them, and limits on changes schools must make.

resources.title: Know Your Rights: Pregnant or Parenting? Title IX Protects You From Discrimination At School
resources.publisher: US Department of Education (Office for Civil Rights)
resources.summary: The US Department of Education explains Title IX protections for pregnant or parenting students at federally funded schools: the right to stay in classes and activities, excused absences while a doctor says necessary, protection from harassment, and the right to file a complaint.

resources.title: Know your overdraft options
resources.summary: The US Consumer Financial Protection Bureau explains three ways to reduce overdraft fees: opting out of debit and ATM overdraft coverage, linking a savings account to cover shortfalls, or asking for a line of credit, plus tips like balance alerts to avoid overdrawing your account.

resources.title: Checklist for Opening a Bank or Credit Union Account
resources.summary: A CFPB checklist for opening a US bank or credit union account: getting fee and service recommendations, making an initial deposit of $25 to $100, understanding minimum balance requirements, and the identification documents needed, such as a driver's license, passport, Social Security number or ITIN.

resources.title: Consumer Guide to Selecting a Lower-Risk Account
resources.summary: The US CFPB's guide helps consumers choose a checking or prepaid account that won't let them spend beyond their balance, avoiding overdraft fees and negative checking-account reports, and lists questions to ask about fees, features and tradeoffs before selecting a lower-risk account.

resources.title: Consumer Resource Center
resources.length: Hub page linking to multiple tools and guides
resources.summary: The FDIC's Consumer Resource Center is a hub for free US financial education: Bank Find to locate FDIC-insured institutions, deposit insurance coverage explained, the Electronic Deposit Insurance Estimator to calculate coverage, the Money Smart financial education program, fraud protection tips, and monthly FDIC Consumer News.

resources.title: How to choose a bank account
resources.summary: MoneyHelper's UK guide to choosing a bank account: listing common features like debit cards and bill payments, optional perks such as cashback or interest-free overdrafts, checking eligibility criteria, comparing deals, and alternatives like basic bank accounts or credit union accounts if you're refused one.

resources.title: Payments, transfers and cheques in the EU
resources.language: English (also available in other EU languages)
resources.summary: Your Europe explains EU rules on payments, transfers and cheques: banks must charge the same rate for euro payments across the EU as for domestic ones, no card surcharges, fraud liability capped at €50, and blocked card amounts that must be released promptly.

resources.title: How to sort a problem with a payment
resources.summary: MoneyHelper's UK guide to fixing a payment problem: Section 75 claims on credit card purchases over £100, chargeback protection for debit cards and PayPal within 120 to 180 days, reporting wrong bank transfers within two working days, and escalating complaints to the Financial Ombudsman Service.

resources.title: Section 75 and chargeback protection
resources.summary: MoneyHelper explains UK Section 75 protection on credit card purchases of £100 to £30,000, covering goods not supplied or misrepresented, and debit card chargeback claims within 120 days, including how some Buy Now Pay Later purchases and PayPal payments can also qualify.

resources.title: What is a remittance transfer and what are my rights?
resources.summary: The US CFPB explains rights for remittance transfers, electronic transfers over $15 sent abroad through a provider: receiving fee, exchange rate and delivery information upfront, receipts in your language, 30 minutes to cancel after paying, and 180 days to report a mistake for investigation.

resources.title: Buying and using insurance and pensions products
resources.publisher: European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority (EIOPA)
resources.summary: EIOPA's hub guides EU consumers through buying, tracking, claiming and cancelling insurance and pension products: where to purchase them, what documentation to expect, monitoring investment-linked contracts, making a claim, complaining about a provider, and the cooling-off period for cancellation.

resources.title: Insurance products in the EU
resources.language: English (also available in other EU languages)
resources.summary: Your Europe explains EU rules for buying insurance products: the right to shop across borders, receiving a standardised Insurance Product Information Document before signing, knowing whether the seller is an agent or broker, and the right to buy a product without its attached insurance policy.

resources.title: Insurance
resources.length: Hub page linking to dozens of articles
resources.summary: MoneyHelper's UK insurance hub covers car, home, travel, health and life insurance, plus income protection and critical illness cover, with articles on choosing a policy, using an insurance broker, comparing deals with price comparison sites, and what to do if a provider rejects your claim.

resources.title: What is insurance?
resources.summary: A CFPB student handout from its Building Blocks financial education series explains what insurance is and how it reduces financial risk: premiums, deductibles, policyholders versus the insured, and common types including health, life, disability, auto and homeowner's or renter's insurance.

resources.title: Here and Now! Education for Sustainable Consumption: Recommendations and Guidelines
resources.summary: UNEP's 2010 publication provides recommendations and guidelines for education on sustainable consumption, in two parts: a rationale and action-plan suggestions for policymakers, and practical guidance for educational authorities, teacher trainers, teachers and educators to bring sustainable consumption into classrooms internationally.

resources.title: YouthXchange Training Kit on Responsible Consumption: Towards Sustainable Lifestyles: The Guide
resources.summary: UNEP and UNESCO's YouthXchange training kit helps trainers teach young people worldwide about sustainable consumption, using statistics, case studies, games and real company examples organised under youth-oriented themes like clothing, leisure and travel, aiming to shape consumption habits among tomorrow's decision makers.

resources.title: Tips on Saving Money and Energy in Your Home (Energy Saver Guide)
resources.summary: The US Department of Energy's 56-page guide covers home energy audits, weatherizing and insulating your home, efficient heating and cooling, energy-saving home design, renewable electricity and appliances, renters' options, and fuel-efficient and electric vehicles, with tips to cut utility bills.

resources.title: Consumer Guide to Home Energy Assessments
resources.summary: The US Department of Energy's 2-page guide explains DIY and professional home energy assessments: how to spot air leaks yourself, blower door tests and thermographic scans used by certified assessors, what to prepare before an assessment, and typical costs of $250 to $600 or more.

resources.title: Consumers - Energy Efficient Products
resources.summary: The European Commission explains EU Ecodesign and Energy Label rules that help consumers choose efficient products, save an average of €290 a year on household energy bills, and use the EPREL database to compare product models by energy use, water consumption and spare-parts availability.

resources.title: European Energy Consumers' Rights: What You Gain as an Energy Consumer from European Legislation
resources.licence: © European Union, 2014. Reproduction authorised provided the source is acknowledged.
resources.summary: A European Commission leaflet lists ten EU energy consumer rights: connection to the grid, free choice and easy switching of supplier, clear contract information, accurate billing, help using energy efficiently, protection for vulnerable customers, complaint resolution, an energy performance certificate, and a national contact point.

resources.title: Energy in Buildings
resources.summary: The Open University's free OpenLearn course examines energy use in UK buildings: how houses lose heat, U-value calculations for windows and insulation, factors affecting heating system efficiency, CO2 emissions of different heating systems, and lighting calculations, rated Level 3 (Advanced), about 10 hours of study.

resources.title: Introduction to Environmental Sciences and Sustainability
resources.publisher: Emily P. Harris, University of West Florida (Open Textbook Library)
resources.summary: An open textbook (CC BY licensed) from the University of West Florida covering environmental science and sustainability in 14 chapters, including water availability, food and hunger, conventional and sustainable energy, and solid and hazardous waste, designed for an introductory college science course.
